analysis.title: Houlihan Lokey Inc. (HLI): Better revenue and non-comp discipline, incrementally constructive restructuring outlook
key_insights: HLI reported adjusted F2Q27 EPS of $1.85, above GSe/Visible Alpha consensus of $1.66/$1.65, driven by stronger revenue and margins.
Total revenue came in 9% above GSe/consensus, on Corporate Finance revenue 14% above the Street, partly offset by Restructuring 4% below and Valuation (FVA) 1% below.
Operating margin was 25.3%, about 115bps above consensus, on a non-comp ratio about 135bps lower. Non-comp expense was 9% lower QoQ and 2% below the Street despite 35% sequential revenue growth.
GS expects a positive market reaction to the beat and the constructive outlook across businesses, especially Financial Restructuring.

Management struck a cautiously optimistic M&A tone, citing rising transaction demand from sponsors and stronger than normal F2H27E seasonality. It noted possible headwinds from rates and lingering geopolitical uncertainty.

Corporate Finance revenue of $481mn was up 59% sequentially, with a return to growth across all geographies and industries except technology and healthcare. Transactions continued to close despite a higher rate environment.

Management's restructuring outlook is incrementally more positive through 2028, driven by record backlogs, geopolitical disruption, higher rates and the coming maturity wall. It expects stronger F2H27 revenue than F1H27 and software dislocation to lift revenue in calendar 2027E/28E.
Restructuring revenue of $118mn was 4% below consensus and down 12% YoY.
FVA revenue of $93mn was up 7% YoY and 4% QoQ, 1% below the Street. Management is constructive on further growth in its non-cyclical portfolio valuations business.
GS raises FY27E/28E/29E revenue by 3%/1%/1% and operating margins by about 0.4pp/0.2pp/0.1pp. Management maintained FY27E non-comp dollar growth guidance similar to FY26's 11%.
HLI continues to highlight a strong acquisition pipeline. Advisory MDs rose by 7 QoQ, or +10% YoY.

GS raises its 12-month price target 7% to $164 (from $153) by rolling forward its Q5-Q8 P/E multiple one quarter and lifting it 0.5x to 18.5x on higher market multiples. Rating stays BUY, with 19.4% upside from $137.38.

market_movers.rationale: Beat on Corporate Finance revenue and non-comp discipline, plus a more constructive restructuring outlook. Target rises 7% from $153 on a higher P/E multiple of 18.5x.

tension_points.bull_case: Management sees record restructuring backlogs, geopolitical disruption, higher rates and the maturity wall driving stronger F2H27 and calendar 2027/28 revenue. Sponsor appetite to transact is recovering and Corporate Finance has returned to growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Restructuring revenue missed consensus and fell 12% YoY. Higher rates and lingering geopolitical uncertainty could be M&A headwinds, and large M&A deals could keep outperforming.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Slower M&A activity or an inability to complete the backlog, per the report's downside risks.

theme_stances.key_argument: Stronger Corporate Finance results and an incrementally constructive restructuring outlook support higher estimates.
